panels.title: The third pillar
points: It is a right of the poor in our wealth

panels.title: Who pays?
points: A Muslim with savings above nisab
Kept for one full Islamic year

model.title: Example: Amina's savings are £2,000, above nisab, for a full year. How much zakah?

blocks.text: Zakah is 2.5%: find 10%, then a quarter of it. These are example amounts held for a lunar year above the nisab.

keywords.def: a set part of savings given each year to those in need
the minimum amount of wealth before zakah is due
two and a half pounds in every hundred

questions.a: It purifies the giver's wealth and heart from greed; it helps the poor and needy.

questions.q: Work out zakah on £400 (example, above nisab).

questions.a: The minimum wealth before zakah is due
options: The minimum wealth before zakah is due

questions.q: Zakah calculator on the pupil PDF (example amounts): work out 2.5% of £1,000, £3,000 and £600, then write one sentence on why zakah is a pillar.
questions.a: £25, £75, £15; zakah is a pillar because Allah commands it and it cares for the poor

questions.q: Extend: why must the wealth be kept a full year?
questions.a: Zakah is a yearly duty on savings that have stayed above nisab for a year.

questions.q: Stretch: Yusuf's savings are below nisab. Does he pay zakah? Can he still give?
questions.a: No zakah is due, but he can give sadaqah.

questions.q: What is the rate of zakah on savings?
Zakah is the ... pillar of Islam.
Think again: can giving make wealth grow?
questions.a: Yes: Allah blesses and purifies wealth when zakah is given.
